526	## 6. Expressions
527	
528	**Nothing is evaluated unless it is in braces.** `a + b` is the string
529	`"a + b"`, and `{a + b}` is `3` when `a` is 1 and `b` is 2. The braces keep the
530	compiler simple, and they mean an unrecognized word never silently falls back
531	to being a string.
532	
533	- Inside the braces, **bare words are symbols**. Quote string operands:
534	  `{2 + "Hello"}` gives `"2Hello"`. An unknown name is `unresolved-symbol`.
535	  List literals inside braces follow the same rule: `{["A", "B"] + ["C"]}`.
536	- **Keep the whole expression inside the braces.** `{this.flag && false}`
537	  evaluates; `{this.flag} && false` is text around an expression.
538	- **Braces that don't hold a valid expression are an error**, and so is an
539	  empty `{}` or `${}`. To write braces as text, escape them: `\ {1 +} \`.
540	- **Forward references resolve.** Unresolved references are errors, and so are
541	  cyclic values: `A: {B}` together with `B: {A}` fails with `cyclic-value`.
542	- Collections are copied by value:
543	
544	  ```piton
545	  myList: [1, 2, 3]
546	  myDictionary:
547	      list: {myList}
548	  newList: {myDictionary.list + [4, 5, 6]}
549	  ```
550	
551	  `newList` is `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`.
552	- **Anchors are copied too, but the copy still knows which anchor it is.** If
553	  `x` is `{Foo}`, then `{x == Foo}` is `true`, `${x}` is `"Foo"`, and `x`
554	  passes a `Foo` type constraint. The output is still a copy of Foo's content.
555	  For a link instead of a copy, use `@{Foo}`.
556	
557	### 6.1 The four expression forms
558	
559	| Form | Name | Result |
560	| --- | --- | --- |
561	| `{expr}` | Standard | The intrinsic value with its type preserved. An anchor serializes as its resolved content (a copy that keeps its identity). |
562	| `${expr}` | String | Converts the result to a string. |
563	| `#{expr}` | Numeric | Converts the result to a number. |
564	| `@{expr}` | Reference | A reference to an anchor or a property on one. Renders as a link or path, never as the content. |
565	
566	Use `@{X}` to point at another document, `{X}` to embed a copy of it, and
567	`${X}` to mention it by name.
568	
569	### 6.2 Expressions in text
570	
571	If the whole value is one expression (`total: {a + b}`), it keeps its type. If
572	there is other text around it:
573	
574	- `${x}` turns the result into a string, so the whole value is a string.
575	- `{x}` with a simple value drops it into the text: `Total: {a + b}` is
576	  `"Total: 3"`.
577	- `{x}` with a list, dictionary or anchor copies it in and **turns the
578	  property into an implicit list**. `See {Foo} for details` becomes a list of
579	  `"See"`, a copy of Foo, and `"for details"`.
580	- `@{x}` puts in a reference, which ends up as a link or a path.
581	
582	### 6.3 Conversions
583	
584	`${}` (string):
585	
586	- A string is returned unchanged. A number becomes its text form. A boolean
587	  becomes `true` or `false`. Null becomes `null`.
588	- An anchor becomes its name as written in the source: `${Child}` gives
589	  `"Child"`, and `${self}` gives the name of the current most-derived anchor.
590	  It is not turned into a title.
591	- A named list or dictionary becomes its name: `Anchor.propertyName`, or just
592	  the variable name at the top of a file. So if `tags` is a top-level list,
593	  `${tags}` is `"tags"`.
594	- A list or dictionary with no name (`${[1, 2]}`) is `no-string-form`.
595	- **`${}` never pulls in the contents** of a list, dictionary or anchor, only
596	  its name. For the contents use `{x}`; for a link use `@{x}`. In
597	  `Metadata.pi`:
598	
599	  ```piton
600	  export anchor Metadata:
601	      name: Piton
602	      version:: string: 1.0
603	
604	  export byName: Information about Piton ${Metadata}
605	  export byValue: Information about Piton {Metadata}
606	  export byLink: Information about Piton @{Metadata}
607	  ```
608	
609	  `byName` is `"Information about Piton Metadata"`, `byValue` is
610	  `["Information about Piton", {"name": "Piton", "version": "1.0"}]`, and
611	  `byLink` is `"Information about Piton ./Metadata.json:Metadata"` (in
612	  Markdown, `[Metadata](./Metadata.md#metadata)`).
613	- The result is never re-parsed as source.
614	- In structured output the value stays a string; whatever escaping the output
615	  format needs is applied when it is serialized.
616	
617	`#{}` (numeric):
618	
619	- A number is returned unchanged. A string converts only if the **entire**
620	  string is a valid Piton numeric literal: `#{"42"}` gives `42`. It is never
621	  evaluated as an expression.
622	- Booleans, null, collections and anchors are rejected (`not-a-number`).
623	- The result is a number you can keep computing with. In structured output it
624	  stays numeric; it becomes text only when the output format needs text.
625	
626	### 6.4 Operators
627	
628	| Group | Operators | Rules |
629	| --- | --- | --- |
630	| Access | `.` | Property access on dictionaries and anchors. |
631	| Arithmetic | `+ - * / %` | Numbers only. Division or modulo by zero is an error. `%` keeps the sign of the left side: `{-7 % 3}` is `-1`. |
632	| Comparison | `== != < <= > >=` | The result is a boolean. `==` and `!=` work on every type (see below). `< <= > >=` work on numbers and on strings (by Unicode code point); anything else, or a number against a string, is an error. |
633	| Logical | `&& \|\| !` | Booleans only. **There is no truthiness**; anything else is `invalid-operand`. **No short-circuiting**: both sides are always evaluated and must be booleans, so `{true \|\| 5}` and `{false && 1 / 0 == 1}` are both errors. |
634	| Conditional | `cond ? a : b` | The condition must be a boolean (`invalid-condition`). Only the selected branch is evaluated. Chainable in either slot. |
635	| Concatenation / merge | `+` | Dispatches on the operand types (table below). |
636	| Duplicate merge | `++` | Lists: joined in order, duplicates kept. Dictionaries: deep merge (nested dictionaries on both sides are merged all the way down; otherwise the right side wins). Strings: joined with a line break. |
637	
638	**`+` dispatch:**
639	
640	| Left | Right | Operation |
641	| --- | --- | --- |
642	| number | number | addition |
643	| string | simple | concatenation |
644	| simple | string | concatenation |
645	| string | list, dictionary or anchor | implicit list |
646	| list, dictionary or anchor | string | implicit list |
647	| list | list | merge: joined in order, duplicates removed, last occurrence kept |
648	| dictionary | dictionary | shallow merge: keys from both, right side wins |
649	| anything else | | compiler error |
650	
651	- Concatenation stringifies the non-string side by the `${}` rules:
652	  `{2 + "Hello"}` is `"2Hello"` and `{"Enabled: " + true}` is
653	  `"Enabled: true"`.
654	- A list, dictionary or anchor is never stringified by `+`. If `tags` is
655	  `[a, b]`, `{"Tags: " + tags}` is `["Tags: ", ["a", "b"]]`. Use `${tags}` if
656	  you want the name.
657	- `{["A", "B", "C", "D"] + ["A", "B", "C"]}` is `[D, A, B, C]`;
658	  `{["A", "B", "C", "D"] ++ ["A", "B", "C"]}` is `[A, B, C, D, A, B, C]`.
659	- `{1 + true}`, `{null + 1}` and `{1 ++ 2}` are errors (`invalid-operand`).
660	
661	**Equality:** lists and dictionaries are equal if everything inside them is
662	equal. Anchors are equal only if they are the same anchor, and references only
663	if they point at the same thing.
664	
665	**Precedence** (higher rows go first; the same row goes left to right, except
666	the ternary, which goes right to left; parentheses change the order):
667	
668	| Precedence | Operators |
669	| --- | --- |
670	| 1 (highest) | `.` |
671	| 2 | `!` |
672	| 3 | `*` `/` `%` |
673	| 4 | `+` `-` `++` |
674	| 5 | `<` `<=` `>` `>=` |
675	| 6 | `==` `!=` |
676	| 7 | `&&` |
677	| 8 | `\|\|` |
678	| 9 (lowest) | `? :` |
679	
680	So `{1 + 2 == 3 && !false}` is `{((1 + 2) == 3) && (!false)}`, and
681	`{a ? b : c ? d : e}` is `{a ? b : (c ? d : e)}`.
682	
683	**Control flow:** the ternary is the only conditional, and the only operator
684	that evaluates just one side. There are no loops and no functions.
685	
686	**Declaration operators:** `:` (assignment) and `::` (type annotation) are
687	documented as operators in `spec/scope/language/operators/declaration/`
688	(`DeclarationOperators`), but they are not expression operators: they aren't in
689	`allOperators`, the precedence table, or any type's `supportedOperators`.
690	
691	**Why `+` and `++`:** on lists, `+` behaves like a set (duplicates removed,
692	last kept) and `++` like a list (duplicates kept). The spec explains this in
693	`ConcatenationOperators.setsAndLists`.
694	
695	### 6.5 References `@{}`
696	
697	- The expression must identify an anchor or **a property on one**
698	  (`@{Button}`, `@{Button.color}`). Anything else is `invalid-reference`.
699	  **A plain list or dictionary at the top of a file can't be referenced**; to
700	  link to it, put it in an anchor.
701	- The referenced anchor joins the compilation dependency graph (for a
702	  property, the anchor it is on), so it gets compiled and emitted.
703	- References are resolved separately for each output target, through the
704	  renderer or the framework adapter on top of it. If a target cannot represent
705	  a reference, that is an error. A reference never silently becomes an
706	  embedded copy or a plain name.
707	- References compare with `==` and `!=`: equal if they point at the same
708	  thing.
709	- How each renderer writes one:
710	
711	  | Renderer | Reference to `Button` | Reference to `Button.color` |
712	  | --- | --- | --- |
713	  | JSON | `"./Button.json:Button"` | `"./Button.json:Button.color"` |
714	  | YAML | `./Button.yaml:Button` | `./Button.yaml:Button.color` |
715	  | Markdown | `[Button](./Button.md#button)` | `[Button.color](./Button.md#color)` |
716	
717	  JSON and YAML write the path to the other output file (relative to this
718	  one), a colon, and the dot path. Markdown writes a relative link with the
719	  anchor's name (or `Anchor.property`) as the link text, and a fragment for the
720	  specific anchor or property heading. The link is **lazy**: the content is
721	  not inlined, and an agent follows it only when the work touches what it
722	  describes.
723	- A Markdown link you write yourself (`[Button](./Button.md)`) is plain text,
724	  not a reference. Only `@{...}` is resolved and checked.

726	## 7. Modules and reuse
727	
728	### 7.1 Export and import
729	
730	```piton
731	export pi: 3.14
732	myVariable: 42
733	export anchor MyAnchor:
734	    description: This is my anchor
735	```
736	
737	`myVariable` is not exported, so no other file can import it.
738	
739	```piton
740	from ./FirstFile import pi, MyAnchor
741	from ./FirstFile import pi SliceOf, MyAnchor MyAliasedAnchor
742	from /subdir/subdir/file import AnAnchor
743	from ./path/to/directory import MyAnchor
744	from .. import Something
745	from my-package import MyAnchor
746	from @piton/belay import ClaudeCodeAdapter
747	from ./file import
748	    FirstThing,
749	    SecondThing,
750	    ThirdThing
751	```
752	
753	- Paths are relative to the current file. A path that starts with `/` is
754	  relative to the `root` in `piton.config.pi`.
755	- **The `.pi` extension is optional**, and `piton format` removes it.
756	- A bare `.` or `..` points at the `index.pi` in that directory. A directory
757	  path resolves to its `index.pi`.
758	- Only exported names can be imported (`unresolved-export`). A missing module
759	  is `unresolved-module`.
760	- Aliasing is `Name Alias`, with no `as`. After aliasing, only the alias is in
761	  scope (`pi` above is available only as `SliceOf`).
762	- `export Name` on its own line re-exports something already declared or
763	  imported.
764	- **Circular imports are allowed.** Mutually referencing values are fine as
765	  long as every value settles:
766	
767	  ```piton
768	  anchor A:
769	      description: This anchor talks about ${B}
770	
771	  anchor B:
772	      description: This anchor talks about ${A}
773	  ```
774	
775	  This works because both settle to strings (the anchor names). `A: {B}` with
776	  `B: {A}` cannot resolve, so it fails. The only cycles that are errors are
777	  ones that can't resolve and an anchor that ends up extending itself.
778	
779	### 7.2 Index files and re-export
780	
781	An `index.pi` file exposes a directory as a module:
782	
783	```piton
784	from ./MyAnchor import MyAnchor
785	export MyAnchor
786	```
787	
788	The shorter forms:
789	
790	```piton
791	from ./MyAnchor export MyAnchor
792	from ./MyAnchor export *
793	from ./MyAnchor export MyAnchor MyAliasedAnchor, MyOtherAnchor MyOtherAliasedAnchor
794	```
795	
796	**Importing a name into an index does not re-export it.** When an index uses
797	`import`, consumers must import leaf anchors from their own files, or the
798	index must `export` them.
799	
800	### 7.3 `use`
801	
802	`use` brings the **user-defined keywords** a module exports into scope, and
803	nothing else. `from ... import` never brings keywords.
804	
805	```piton
806	use ./CustomKeywords
807	
808	my-custom-keyword Wow:
809	    description: amazing
810	```
811	
812	- Valid forms include `use ./CustomKeywords`, `use .`, `use ../cli`,
813	  `use my-package`, `use my-package/MyAnchor` and `use @piton/belay`.
814	- A file that declares with a keyword *and* names its abstract as a type needs
815	  both lines: `use ./Foo` and `from ./Foo import Foo`.
816	- Using a keyword without `use` gives `unknown-keyword`.
817	
818	### 7.4 Formatting of imports
819	
820	`piton format` sorts the imports: in each run of import lines, the `use`
821	lines come first, then the `from` lines, each sorted by path, and the names in
822	each line are sorted too. A blank line keeps two runs apart. It breaks an
823	import or `from ... export` line across lines when it has more than 2 items or
824	runs past 80 columns, and drops the `.pi` extension from paths. You can write
825	those line breaks yourself on either kind of line.

827	## 8. Anchors
828	
829	An anchor is a named structural declaration that can take part in
830	inheritance, typing, exports and composition. It is the core building block of
831	Piton, something like a class that is never instantiated. An *object* is a
832	value. An *anchor* is a declaration.
833	
834	```piton
835	export anchor MyFirstAnchor:
836	    whatIsAnAnchor:
837	        An anchor is a kind of object or document that is structured via
838	        properties and values.
839	    listTypes:
840	        - List types
841	        - are supported.
842	    numberTypes: {3.14 - 3.14}
843	    booleanTypes: true
844	    nullType: null
845	    booleanOperatorsAnd: {this.booleanTypes && false}
846	    booleanOperatorsOr: {this.booleanTypes || false}
847	```
848	
849	Compiled to JSON, an anchor becomes an object of its resolved properties
850	(`numberTypes` is `0`, `booleanOperatorsAnd` is `false`,
851	`booleanOperatorsOr` is `true`). Valid anchor keys follow the dictionary rules.
852	
853	### 8.1 Structural inheritance
854	
855	`anchor Child extends A, B:` copies the properties of every base and then
856	applies the child's own. On a collision, **the right-most base wins, and the
857	child beats every base.** Type constraints from bases follow the same rule
858	(abstracts have their own, 8.4). This is structural inheritance, not
859	polymorphism.
860	
861	```piton
862	anchor FirstBaseAnchor:
863	    firstBaseAnchorProperty: Hello from the First Base Anchor
864	    description: Description from FirstBaseAnchor
865	
866	anchor SecondBaseAnchor:
867	    secondBaseAnchorProperty: Hello from the Second Base Anchor
868	    description: Description from SecondBaseAnchor
869	
870	anchor ChildAnchor extends FirstBaseAnchor, SecondBaseAnchor:
871	    childAnchorProperty: Hello from Child Anchor
872	```
873	
874	`ChildAnchor.description` is `"Description from SecondBaseAnchor"`.
875	
876	- An anchor can't extend itself, directly or through others
877	  (`inheritance-cycle`). Extending something that is not an anchor is
878	  `invalid-base`; an unknown base is `unresolved-base`.
879	- A child can't redeclare an inherited constraint (4.3).
880	
881	### 8.2 `super`
882	
883	`super` is everything the anchor inherits, merged the same way as property
884	inheritance: left to right, last in line wins. **So if the last base doesn't
885	have the property, `super` still finds it on an earlier one.**
886	
887	```piton
888	anchor Left:
889	    d: from-left
890	
891	anchor Right:
892	    other: x
893	
894	anchor Child extends Left, Right:
895	    d: ${super.d} plus child
896	```
897	
898	`Child.d` is `"from-left plus child"`. If no base has the property, that is a
899	compiler error. Use `${super.x}` to extend prose, and a `+ {super.items}`
900	line to extend a list (section 5).
901	
902	### 8.3 `self` and `this`
903	
904	- **`self`** means the most-derived anchor, and it travels down the hierarchy.
905	  When a base writes `${self.name}`, a child compiled from it shows the child's
906	  name.
907	- **`this`** is pinned to the anchor that lexically contains the expression.
908	  When a base writes `${this.name}`, it always shows the base's own value,
909	  including in anchors that inherit it. When a child overrides the property,
910	  the override's own `this` refers to the child.
911	
912	```piton
913	anchor Base:
914	    name: Base Anchor
915	    baseDescription: This is ${this.name}
916	
917	anchor MidChild extends Base:
918	    name: MidChild Anchor
919	    baseDescription: Override on baseDescription ${this.name}
920	    childDescription: This is ${self.name}
921	
922	anchor FinalChild extends MidChild:
923	    name: FinalChild Anchor
924	```
925	
926	`FinalChild` is `{"name": "FinalChild Anchor", "baseDescription": "Override on baseDescription MidChild Anchor", "childDescription": "This is FinalChild Anchor"}`.
927	
928	- `self` only travels through inheritance. Reading a property from another
929	  anchor gives that anchor's value, with `self` being that anchor:
930	
931	  ```piton
932	  anchor Precedence:
933	      note: ${self} rules apply
934	
935	  anchor Addition:
936	      copied: ${Precedence.note}
937	  ```
938	
939	  `Addition.copied` is `"Precedence rules apply"`.
940	- `this` and `self` always mean an anchor, never a dictionary. Even inside a
941	  nested dictionary, they mean the anchor it is in.
942	- Using `self`, `this` or `super` outside an anchor is an error
943	  (`invalid-self`, `invalid-this`, `invalid-super`).
944	
945	### 8.4 Abstract anchors
946	
947	```piton
948	abstract anchor Construct:
949	    description:: string
950	    prompt:: string
951	
952	abstract anchor Skill extends Construct as skill:
953	    useWhen:: string
954	
955	skill Review:
956	    description: Reviews code
957	    prompt: Review the diff
958	    useWhen: Asked for a review
959	```
960	
961	- An abstract anchor defines a shape without necessarily providing values. It
962	  **never compiles on its own** and produces no output. A concrete anchor that
963	  extends it *implements* it and must give every required property a value
964	  (`unimplemented-property`). A property with a default is optional (4.3).
965	- If nothing implements an abstract, you get a warning
966	  (`unimplemented-abstract`), unless it's exported, since another file or
967	  project may implement it.
968	- An abstract may extend another abstract. The implementer has to fill in the
969	  required properties from the whole chain.
970	- **An anchor can implement more than one abstract**, even ones that share a
971	  base, and it can extend concrete anchors as well. If two abstracts constrain
972	  the same property to types that don't overlap at all (say string and
973	  number), that is `conflicting-abstracts`. If they overlap, the right-most
974	  one wins. Constraints from concrete bases follow normal inheritance.
975	- Good practice is to export an abstract with a keyword. The keyword's anchor
976	  always goes last in the chain, so it wins (8.6).
977	- All the special constraints (`simple`, `complex`, `any`, `[]`, `extends`)
978	  work inside abstracts.
979	- **Anchor-type constraints:**
980	
981	  ```piton
982	  abstract anchor A:
983	      description:: string
984	
985	  abstract anchor B extends A:
986	      name:: string
987	
988	  abstract anchor C:
989	      listOfA:: A[]
990	      listOfB:: B[]
991	      listOfExtendsA:: extends A[]
992	  ```
993	
994	  A plain anchor type only matches anchors that **directly implement** it, so
995	  `listOfA` takes anchors implementing `A`, and something implementing `B`
996	  does not fit even though `B extends A`. When an anchor has several
997	  abstracts, the one that counts is the winning one: the keyword's abstract,
998	  or else the right-most. `extends A[]` accepts any **concrete** anchor whose
999	  inheritance chain includes `A`, so implementers of `A` or `B` both fit.
1000	- Extra properties a concrete anchor adds beyond the abstract's shape are
1001	  kept. Belay relies on this: extra properties on a construct are serialized
1002	  into the generated guidance.
1003	
1004	### 8.5 Value-less declarations
1005	
1006	`name:: type` with no value is only allowed inside an abstract anchor, where
1007	it declares a required property. Anywhere else it is `missing-value`, and an
1008	empty `name:` anywhere is `empty-value`.
1009	
1010	### 8.6 User-defined keywords
1011	
1012	`as` gives an anchor a keyword alias. Declaring with the keyword is syntactic
1013	sugar for `extends`:
1014	
1015	```piton
1016	anchor MyAnchor as my-anchor:
1017	    description: This is a description of my anchor
1018	
1019	anchor OtherBase:
1020	    description: Other Base
1021	
1022	my-anchor ChildAnchor extends OtherBase:
1023	    description:
1024	        ${super.description}
1025	        My additional description
1026	```
1027	
1028	- `my-anchor ChildAnchor:` is exactly `anchor ChildAnchor extends MyAnchor:`.
1029	  Keywords exist to mark certain base anchors as the fundamental units of a
1030	  design.
1031	- `my-anchor ChildAnchor extends OtherBase:` is exactly
1032	  `anchor ChildAnchor extends OtherBase, MyAnchor:`. **The keyword's anchor is
1033	  the last base, so it wins collisions** with what is in `extends`. Here
1034	  `ChildAnchor.description` starts with "This is a description of my anchor".
1035	- Only one keyword per anchor, but `extends` can add more bases.
1036	- A keyword can be built on another keyword:
1037	  `export abstract operator ArithmeticOperator as arithmetic-operator:`
1038	  declares with the `operator` keyword and defines `arithmetic-operator`.
1039	- To declare with a keyword, a file must `use` the module that exports it.
1040	- A reserved word can't be a keyword (`reserved-keyword`).
1041	
1042	## 9. Compilation model
1043	
1044	- **`piton compile <file>`** produces one object with **one key per export**.
1045	  Anything not exported is left out, and so are abstract anchors. (The JSON
1046	  examples in the spec skip the export wrapper to stay short.)
1047	- **`piton build`** compiles the project. Everything exported from the entry
1048	  file is compiled, whether or not anything uses it, plus anything those
1049	  exports reference, so the links have somewhere to go. Everything else is
1050	  left out, and abstract anchors never compile.
1051	- **Renderers** decide the format: `json` (default), `yaml` or `markdown`.
1052	  Frameworks add adapters on top; Belay's adapters build on the Markdown
1053	  renderer.
1054	- **Markdown serialization** (used by the Markdown renderer and Belay; the
1055	  worked examples are in `spec/scope/belay/Compilation.pi`,
1056	  `MarkdownSerialization`):
1057	  - Anchor and property names become word-separated title headings.
1058	    `myProperty` becomes `My Property`, `t1` becomes `T 1`, and runs of
1059	    capitals are not split (`whatIsAType` becomes `What Is AType`). Heading
1060	    depth follows nesting, and bold labels (`**G**`) take over past level 6.
1061	  - **Every property of an anchor gets a heading**, even one holding a single
1062	    `false` or `42`, with the value under it.
1063	  - A **pure dictionary** is one whose every value is a simple value (string,
1064	    number, boolean, null) or another pure dictionary: no lists and no mixed
1065	    content anywhere inside. It is written as-is, indentation-structured,
1066	    inside a code fence, and its keys don't become headings, including when
1067	    it's embedded in mixed content.
1068	  - A dictionary that isn't pure, and any mixed content, gets a heading per
1069	    key instead.
1070	  - **Strings count as simple values, even long prose**, so a dictionary whose
1071	    values are all prose is fenced. To get a heading per key, start the block
1072	    with a line of prose before the keys, or make at least one value a list.
1073	  - Primitives become their text form (`false`, `42`, `null`).
1074	  - Explicit lists become Markdown lists with nested indentation.
1075	  - Mixed lists keep the order of their prose and structure.
1076	  - `{Other}` is serialized as a copy of the anchor's content. Only `@{Other}`
1077	    becomes a link.
1078	- **Interpolation boundary:** Piton evaluates expressions, and the output mode
1079	  decides how the results appear. The distinction between intrinsic values,
1080	  strings and references is preserved. Reference identity is never inferred
1081	  from a display heading.

1083	## 10. Project configuration (`piton.config.pi`)
1084

1162	use and import a bundled framework's keywords and modules whether or not it is

1165	`frameworks:` is what turns on its output.**

1171	## 11. Belay: the agentic framework
1172	
1173	Belay is bundled as `@piton/belay`. It gives Piton a vocabulary for agents and
1174	compiles it into the artifacts that agentic coding tools read. The division of
1175	labour:
1176	
1177	- **Piton** handles parsing, evaluation, imports, exports, inheritance,
1178	  reachability and the renderers.
1179	- **Belay** adds the constructs and the adapters that turn them into files for
1180	  each platform.
1181	- The **consuming platform** executes the result. Successful compilation is
1182	  not proof of correct agent execution.
1183	
1184	Besides the four constructs, Belay provides `belay-config`, the adapters and
1185	the special imports.
1186	
1187	Source authority: lasting changes go into the Piton source. Generated guidance
1188	is derived from the resolved source and configuration, and implementation is
1189	assessed against the specification. The compiler loads the four constructs and
1190	the three adapters from the spec's own `.pi` files
1191	(`spec/scope/belay/anchors/`, `spec/scope/belay/adapters/`), so the compiler
1192	and the spec can't disagree: changing `Skill.pi` changes the framework.
1193	
1194	### 11.1 Configuration
1195	
1196	A project turns on Belay by listing a `belay-config` anchor under
1197	`frameworks`:
1198	
1199	| Field | Meaning |
1200	| --- | --- |
1201	| `codeRoot` | Required. Where the app's code lives, relative to the project config. |
1202	| `shapeRoot` | Optional. Where the shape instructions live. Without it, `BELAY_SHAPE_ROOT` is the project root and nothing is placed by shape. |
1203	| `adapters` | Required. The adapters to build for: `ClaudeCodeAdapter`, `CodexAdapter`, `OpenCodeAdapter`. |
1204	| `crossDiscovery` | Optional. `separate` when each tool's output is deployed apart (every adapter writes its own complete tree); `allow` to accept that OpenCode offers other tools' command skills as ordinary skills. Without it, the enabled tools share one project (11.5). |
1205	| `instructionByteLimit` | Optional number. The instruction byte limit to check against, for targets that have one. |
1206	
1207	Adapter and other paths are relative to the project root (where
1208	`piton.config.pi` lives).

1210	### 11.2 The four constructs
1211	
1212	Every construct extends the abstract `Construct`, whose `description` and
1213	`prompt` are both optional (`:: string:: null: null`). Any other property is
1214	preserved and serialized as Markdown after the prompt.
1215	
1216	| Keyword | Extra required field | Meaning | Output |
1217	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1218	| `instruction` | none | Persistent guidance tied to a code scope. **Its placement is part of its meaning.** | Mapped from `shapeRoot` to the matching `codeRoot` directory (11.3). Instructions for the same scope combine into one guidance file per target. Each is also kept in the compiled shape-reference tree. |
1219	| `skill` | `useWhen:: string` | Instructions the agent loads selectively for one kind of work. | Name from the anchor through the adapter's naming rules. Discovery description is `<description> Use when <useWhen>`. Body is `prompt`, then the extra properties. The platform decides when to load it. |
1220	| `command` | none | An explicit entrypoint that invokes a prompt or directs work through skills. | Name is `x-` plus the normalized name. A native command, or the explicit-invocation equivalent the adapter defines. |
1221	| `agent` | `role:: string` | A role and the instructions for performing it. | Identity is the kebab-case anchor name, unless the target needs another form. The body starts with `You are a <role>`, then the prompt, then the extra properties. |
1222	
1223	- Abstract constructs can supply shared structure. Required fields
1224	  (`useWhen`, `role`) are checked only on concrete constructs, after
1225	  inheritance resolves.
1226	- Description and prompt are left out of the output when missing. **If the
1227	  target needs a description and there isn't one, that is
1228	  `missing-description`**: Claude Code needs one for agents; Codex for skills,
1229	  commands and agents; OpenCode for skills and agents.
1230	- The role introduction is literal: `role: careful reviewer` gives
1231	  `You are a careful reviewer`.
1232	- The skill description is literal too: `description: Reviews code.` with
1233	  `useWhen: asked for a review` gives
1234	  `Reviews code. Use when asked for a review`.

1236	```piton
1237	use @piton/belay
1238	
1239	export skill AnswerSpecQuestions:
1240	    description: Reads the spec and answers questions about it.
1241	    useWhen: asked how part of the specification works
1242	    prompt:
1243	        Read the spec under spec/ and understand the language and features
1244	        before answering.
1245	    reportFormat:
1246	        Save every report as a standalone HTML file.
1247	```

1249	`reportFormat` is an extra property. It renders as a `# Report Format` section
1250	after the prompt.
1251	
1252	**Native options.** Some property names are target metadata rather than prose
1253	and are never serialized into the body: `tools`, `model`, `allowed-tools`,
1254	`mode`, `permission`, `agent`, `model_reasoning_effort` and `sandbox_mode`.
1255	Each adapter supports a subset (11.5). An option the target cannot represent
1256	is `unsupported-option`, and an invalid value is `invalid-option`. How these
1257	are typed is still an open decision (11.7).

1259	### 11.3 Shape mapping (instructions)
1260	
1261	The tree under `shapeRoot` roughly mirrors the tree under `codeRoot`:
1262	
1263	| Source | Existing scope | Generic output |
1264	| --- | --- | --- |
1265	| `spec/shape/components/button/Button.pi` | `src/components/button` | `src/components/button/AGENTS.md` |
1266	| `spec/shape/components/input/Input.pi` and `InputDesign.pi` | `src/components/input` | one combined `src/components/input/AGENTS.md` |
1267	| `spec/shape/components/nonexistent/Component.pi` | `src/components` (walked up) | `src/components/AGENTS.md` |
1268	
1269	- The instruction's directory relative to `shapeRoot` is resolved under
1270	  `codeRoot`. If it is missing, Belay walks upward to the nearest directory
1271	  that exists, **stopping at `codeRoot`**.
1272	- Each adapter uses its own filename: `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code, `AGENTS.md`
1273	  for Codex and OpenCode. The file holds a heading per instruction
1274	  (`# Button Shape`) and its content.
1275	- Falling back to a parent changes placement only. The shape-reference tree
1276	  (`<referenceRoot>/shape/...`) keeps the original relative location.
1277	- What happens to an instruction outside `shapeRoot` is an open decision, so
1278	  the compiler refuses to guess and reports an error
1279	  (`instruction-placement-unspecified`). Keep instructions under `shapeRoot`.
1280	- Loading differs per tool (11.5), so placement does not guarantee the
1281	  instruction is in the initial context.

1283	### 11.4 References and special imports
1284	
1285	- **Emission.** Belay emits only what the build emits: the entry file's
1286	  exports and anything they reference.
1287	- **Reference tree.** Reached anchors are serialized into the adapter's
1288	  `referenceRoot`, **one Markdown file per source module**, keeping the
1289	  module's path under `root`. Each anchor is a heading in its module's file.
1290	  So `spec/components/Button.pi` becomes
1291	  `.claude/reference/components/Button.md`. The reference tree (and its
1292	  `shape/` subdirectory) is a Belay convention, **not a platform discovery
1293	  directory**: never assume a tool loads it. It is reached only through links.
1294	- `@{X}` in any generated file becomes a relative Markdown link to X's heading
1295	  in that tree, with a `#fragment`:
1296	  `[Button](../../reference/components/Button.md#button)`, or
1297	  `[Button.color](../../reference/components/Button.md#color)`. Links stay lazy
1298	  and are never replaced with Claude's eager `@import` syntax.
1299	- **A reference to a skill, command or agent** links to that construct's own
1300	  output, like its `SKILL.md`, and it isn't copied into the reference tree.
1301	- **Special imports.** Each is imported explicitly from `@piton/belay` and
1302	  resolved **at compile time, separately for each adapter and each output
1303	  file**, as a path relative to the generated file that uses it. Interpolate
1304	  them with `${...}`.
1305	
1306	  | Import | Resolves to |
1307	  | --- | --- |
1308	  | `BELAY_COMPILED_SHAPE` | The compiled copy of the shape for the adapter, under its reference directory (`.claude/reference/shape` for Claude Code). Not the same as `BELAY_SHAPE_ROOT`. |
1309	  | `BELAY_AGENT_ROOT` | The agent's directory: `.claude`, `.codex` or `.opencode`. |
1310	  | `BELAY_PROJECT_ROOT` | The project root, where `piton.config.pi` lives. |
1311	  | `BELAY_SHAPE_ROOT` | The configured `shapeRoot`, or the project root if unset. |
1312	  | `BELAY_CODE_ROOT` | The configured `codeRoot`. |
1313	
1314	  ```piton
1315	  use @piton/belay
1316	
1317	  from @piton/belay import BELAY_COMPILED_SHAPE
1318	
1319	  export skill Designer:
1320	      description: Designs components.
1321	      useWhen: asked to design a component
1322	      prompt: Read the shape documents under ${BELAY_COMPILED_SHAPE} first.
1323	  ```

1325	  In `.claude/skills/designer/SKILL.md` that becomes

1335	### 11.5 Adapters
1336	
1337	`@piton/belay` exports `ClaudeCodeAdapter`, `CodexAdapter` and
1338	`OpenCodeAdapter`. Each extends the abstract `belay-agent-adapter`
1339	(`description`, `targetId`, `instructionFile`, `referenceRoot`).
1340	
1341	| | Claude Code (`claude-code`) | Codex (`codex`) | OpenCode (`opencode`) |
1342	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1343	| Instruction file | `CLAUDE.md` | `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` |
1344	| Reference root | `.claude/reference` | `.codex/reference` | `.opencode/reference` |
1345	| Skill | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, YAML frontmatter `name`, `description` | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, same frontmatter | `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Name 1–64 lowercase alphanumerics with single hyphens, matching its directory; description 1–1024 characters. |
1346	| Command | Translated: `.claude/skills/x-<name>/SKILL.md` with `disable-model-invocation: true`, invoked as `/x-<name>` | Translated: `.agents/skills/x-<name>/SKILL.md` plus `agents/openai.yaml` with `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false`, invoked as `$x-<name>` | Native: `.opencode/commands/x-<name>.md`, identity from the filename, invoked as `/x-<name>` |
1347	| Agent | `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, frontmatter `name`, `description`, optional `tools`, `model` | `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `name`, `description`, `developer_instructions` (role, prompt, extras), optional `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode` | `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`, frontmatter `description`, `mode` (`primary`, `subagent` or `all`; always explicit, default `subagent`), optional `model`, `permission`; identity from the filename |
1348	| Native options | agent: `tools`, `model`. skill and command: `allowed-tools`, `model`. | agent: `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`. None for skills or commands. | agent: `mode`, `model`, `permission`. command: `agent`, `model`. None for skills. |
1349	| Loading | Ancestor guidance loads at startup; nested guidance loads when Claude reads in that subtree. | A root-to-working-directory chain is built at run start. A same-directory `AGENTS.override.md` shadows generated guidance (`shadowed-instruction`); an instruction byte limit applies (`instruction-over-budget`). | Searches upward from the working directory and prefers `AGENTS.md` over its `CLAUDE.md` fallback. Nested files are not assumed to load (`unguaranteed-instruction-scope` unless configured). It also discovers Claude and `.agents` skills. |
1350	
1351	Rules for every adapter:
1352	
1353	- **Pipeline:** take the emitted, validated constructs from Piton, build one
1354	  output plan per adapter, resolve instruction placement and reference
1355	  destinations, check shared paths and cross-discovery across the whole plan,
1356	  serialize, validate links, metadata, names and output ownership, then write.
1357	- Every adapter carries `documentationChecked` (currently `2026-09-21`): the
1358	  date its target's documentation was last checked, recorded in the
1359	  manifest's `targets`.
1360	- Constructs are consumed **after** imports and inheritance resolve. Each of
1361	  the four constructs is mapped explicitly for each target.
1362	- An adapter distinguishes native support, translation and unsupported
1363	  behaviour, and fails with an actionable diagnostic when required behaviour
1364	  can't be represented.
1365	- Model and permission settings are applied **only when configured
1366	  explicitly**. Absent settings are omitted so native defaults apply. Native
1367	  options are validated against the target platform version, and role,
1368	  prompt and other prose never get copied into metadata fields.
1369	- **A prompt that requests restraint is not an enforced restriction.** An
1370	  adapter claims enforcement only for controls the platform applies, and never
1371	  translates permissions in a way that silently widens access. Claude's
1372	  `allowed-tools` and subagent `tools` serve different purposes; neither is a
1373	  portable sandbox. Requesting an enforced restriction the adapter can't
1374	  represent is a diagnostic.
1375	- An adapter never silently turns an agent into a skill, or a command into an
1376	  automatically invoked skill, when that changes how it activates.
1377	- Names are normalized before planning, and commands keep the `x-` prefix
1378	  after normalization. Collisions are errors (`name-collision`,
1379	  `output-collision`) unless the artifacts are identical in content,
1380	  reference resolution and activation.
1381	- **Multiple adapters:** the tools read each other's files (Codex and
1382	  OpenCode both read `AGENTS.md`; OpenCode also discovers `.claude/skills` and
1383	  `.agents/skills`), so with several adapters Belay plans one shared project
1384	  and writes each artifact once, where the tools find it:
1385	  - the **first adapter listed owns the one reference tree**, and every
1386	    adapter links into it;
1387	  - an instruction file several adapters place at one path (`AGENTS.md`) is
1388	    **written once**, by the first of them listed;
1389	  - OpenCode **writes no copy of a skill** Claude Code or Codex already
1390	    writes where it discovers it, and links to theirs;
1391	  - a command's `x-` skill that OpenCode would discover is an error
1392	    (`cross-discovery-activation`) unless `opencode.json` hides it with a
1393	    skill permission (`"permission": {"skill": {"x-*": "deny"}}`; the last
1394	    matching pattern decides) or `crossDiscovery` is set;
1395	  - a skill OpenCode finds in two directories (all three adapters enabled)
1396	    is a `cross-target-discovery` warning, since nothing in the project can
1397	    stop it.
1398	
1399	  `crossDiscovery: separate` means each tool's tree is deployed apart: every
1400	  adapter writes its own complete tree, and incompatible writes to one path
1401	  are rejected (`output-collision`). The whole plan is still checked before
1402	  anything is written.
1403	- Generated links (from `@{...}` references) are relative to the file that
1404	  contains them and must point at planned outputs (`broken-reference-link`).
1405	  Markdown links you write in prose are text and are never checked.
1406	- Discovery metadata and body are emitted exactly once. Frontmatter is written
1407	  with a format-aware YAML or TOML encoder. Generated filenames and native
1408	  metadata are checked against the target's schema, and unsupported requested
1409	  capabilities are diagnosed before anything is written.
1410	
1411	Adapter specifics:
1412	
1413	- **Claude Code.** A skill's directory name is its frontmatter `name`. Claude
1414	  Code still reads `.claude/commands/`, but Belay emits commands only as
1415	  skills, never both for one command. Agent identity comes from the
1416	  normalized name, never a rendered heading. `allowed-tools`/`tools` are
1417	  never copied to another platform without a mapping.
1418	- **Codex.** Belay never writes `AGENTS.override.md` to win precedence.
1419	  Guidance below the directory a session starts in is not guaranteed to load.
1420	  The byte limit checked is `instructionByteLimit` (11.1). Commands never use
1421	  deprecated custom prompts or an invented `.codex/commands/`.
1422	  `developer_instructions` is one valid TOML string; a generic `tools` list is
1423	  never mapped to an invented field. Only the standalone custom-agent format is
1424	  targeted. Codex's sandbox and approval settings govern execution and
1425	  guidance can't override them; tool or model settings on a command are
1426	  diagnosed. A command must produce both its files, and an agent's TOML must
1427	  parse with `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`.
1428	- **OpenCode.** Don't assume Claude's nested loading or Codex's chain. Extra
1429	  guidance files go through its explicit `instructions` configuration when a
1430	  deployment needs them, never by loading every nested instruction globally;
1431	  if shape scoping is required and can't be guaranteed, that is an error.
1432	  Unrecognized frontmatter never enforces policy. `model` values are
1433	  provider-qualified. Argument placeholders written in a command prompt are
1434	  kept. `allowed-tools` is never an enforced command setting. Agents use
1435	  `permission`, not the deprecated `tools`, mapped only when the meaning is
1436	  equivalent: allow/ask/deny is not a tool list, and ambiguous conversions are
1437	  rejected.

1473	## 12. Package management
1474	
1475	Packages are git repositories, managed as **vendored dependencies**. Installed
1476	packages are stored inside the project and committed to version control, and
1477	the tooling adds, updates, removes and inspects them. Nothing is fetched at
1478	compile time.
1479	
1480	- **Offering packages.** A repository declares packages with `piton-package`
1481	  anchors (`PitonPackage` from `@piton/packaging`: `name`, `root`,
1482	  `dependencies`). A package anchor can live anywhere in the specbase but must
1483	  be listed under `packages:` in `piton.config.pi`. A package's `root` is
1484	  relative to `piton.config.pi`, like the project's own root. **`packages:` is what the
1485	  repository offers to other projects; a project never installs its own
1486	  packages.** One repository can offer several packages, each with its own
1487	  root and dependencies.
1488	- **Names.** `name` is what the package installs under. It exists because it
1489	  can be kebab-case (`my-package`), which an anchor name can't. Left out, the
1490	  anchor's own name is used. **Package names are flat: no `/`.** Names like
1491	  `@piton/belay` are only for the packages bundled with the compiler.
1492	- **Dependencies.** `dependencies:` lists git URLs, each with an optional
1493	  `commit:`, `tag:` or `branch:` on an indented line beneath it (a dictionary
1494	  item right after the URL). **Only one pin per URL**; more is
1495	  `multiple-pins`. Without a pin, the latest commit on the default branch is
1496	  used. **Pins are strings**: `@piton/config` types them as strings, so
1497	  `tag: 1.0` stays `"1.0"`. Other pin diagnostics are `dangling-pin` and
1498	  `unknown-pin`.
1499	- **Picking packages.** A repository can offer several packages. You get all
1500	  of them unless you list the ones you want with `packages:` under the URL:
1501	  `packages: [ui-kit]`.
1502	- **Project and package dependencies are separate.** The project's apply only
1503	  to the project, and each package declares its own.
1504	- **No nested dependencies.** When two packages need the same package at
1505	  different versions, **the one with the newest commit wins** and a warning is
1506	  shown.
1507	- **Installation.** Each package goes into `tethers/<name>`, next to
1508	  `piton.config.pi`, with the files from its `root`. A repository offering
1509	  `ui-kit` and `my-package` gives `tethers/ui-kit` and `tethers/my-package`.
1510	  Tethering removes every trace of git. A repository that offers no packages
1511	  is installed whole, under the name its URL implies.
1512	- **Importing.** An installed package is a location placeholder:
1513	  `from my-package import X`, `use my-package`, `use my-package/MyAnchor`.
1514	  Normal path resolution applies below it. A missing package is a compiler
1515	  error.
1516	- **Lock file.** `.piton/tether.lock`, next to `piton.config.pi`, keeps each
1517	  tethered package's URL, commit and a hash of its files. `tether` and
1518	  `update` write it, and it is committed with the project.
1519	- **Conflicts.** Before tether, update or any other operation on an installed
1520	  package, the tooling compares its files with the lock file and goes ahead
1521	  only if nothing changed. If the files were edited, it says so and asks the
1522	  user to untether (or `piton update --force` to discard the edits).
1523	
1524	The commands:
1525	
1526	- `piton tether` on its own installs everything in `dependencies`. Given a
1527	  source URL, it adds it to `dependencies` in `piton.config.pi` and installs
1528	  it. `--as <name>` installs under another name.
1529	- `piton update [packages...] [--force] [--diff]` reinstalls from
1530	  `dependencies`, all packages when none are named. `--force` replaces a
1531	  package even if it was edited, discarding the edits with a warning;
1532	  `--diff` prints a coloured unified diff of every file each update changed.
1533	- `piton untether <package>` moves the package from `tethers/` to
1534	  `<root>/untethered/` and rewrites the imports that named it, making it the
1535	  project's own source. `--as <name>` renames it; `--no-rewrite` only moves
1536	  it.
1537	- `piton remove <package>` deletes an installed package and removes it from
1538	  `dependencies`. It refuses if the files were edited or if anything still
1539	  imports the package.

1541	## 13. CLI reference
1542	
1543	Every command prints what it produced first, then a one-line outcome (✓ or
1544	✗), and its problems last: diagnostics, errors and warnings with their help
1545	and notes, then the error and warning count. On a terminal the output is
1546	coloured and paths are marked `+`/`-`; piped or with `NO_COLOR`, it is plain
1547	text and stdout carries the bare results.
1548	
1549	| Command | Behaviour |
1550	| --- | --- |
1551	| `piton check [paths...]` | Validates syntax, imports, references, types, inheritance, composition, exports and circular dependencies, reporting errors and warnings. Writes nothing. Exits 0 when there are no errors and 1 otherwise. Paths are optional files, directories or globs; the default is the project (or every `.pi` file under the working directory when there's no `piton.config.pi`). |
1552	| `piton build [config] [--dry-run]` | Builds the project configured by `piton.config.pi` (or the given config). Writes renderer output to `<output>/<path under root>.<ext>` (defaults: `./dist`, JSON), so `spec/components/Button.pi` becomes `dist/components/Button.json`: the entry file plus every file holding something the entry's exports reference. A registered framework's output replaces it unless the config sets `output` or `renderer`, which asks for both. Records every file in `.piton/manifest.json`. 1553	| `piton compile <path> [--renderer json\|yaml\|markdown] [--write] [--dependencies]` | Compiles one file to stdout (JSON by default): one key per export. `--write` writes `<file>.<ext>` next to each input and is required for globs. `--dependencies` wraps the result as `{"value": "<compiled output as a string>", "dependencies": [absolute source paths]}` so build tools know what to watch; bundled package files are left out. |
